rationale: None of the candidates contains the distinctive Railway Labor Act emergency-board machinery used by the child: findings of an unadjusted railroad labor dispute threatening essential transportation, a board report due within thirty days, and a statutory freeze on changes until thirty days after the report. C05 is the nearest formal analogue because it uses a sequence of factual and statutory recitals followed by numbered operative provisions, but its property-transfer authorization is materially unrelated. C03 and C04 are executive orders with administrative operative clauses, but neither supplies concrete language, sequencing, or machinery plausibly reused in the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS a dispute exists ...; and WHEREAS ... NOW, THEREFORE
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS Section ... provides ...; and WHEREAS ... NOW, THEREFORE, it is hereby ordered as follows
shared_material.explanation: C05 shares a recital-to-operative-order form, but this is generic executive-order drafting and is not accompanied by shared substantive machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The board shall report its findings to the President ... within thirty days
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each governmental officer or agency exercising authority delegated under this order shall ... consult with other agencies or committees
shared_material.explanation: C03 also assigns administrative duties, but it neither creates an emergency investigative board nor uses the child's reporting-and-status-quo sequence.
